r-92c9813fd2e2b9362ac9.title: Prohibition on coordinator-facilitated anticompetitive agreements
r-92c9813fd2e2b9362ac9.requirement: A coordinator may not facilitate a tacit or express agreement among rental property owners that restricts competition concerning residential dwelling units, including by performing a coordinating function.

args.reason: Statutory coordinator status and facilitation of a tacit or express agreement among rental property owners restricting competition are not compiled. Residential ownership or software use alone does not establish these conditions.

Coordinator status is limited by the algorithmic-device and coordinating-function exclusions. Their application to the actor's activities is not compiled; an excluded activity does not exempt every other activity of the actor.

r-92c9813fd2e2b9362ac9.exemptions: Specified institutional facilities are excluded. A government entity setting or limiting residential prices through lawful affordability controls is not a coordinator. Device and coordinating-function exclusions also limit coordinator status.

r-b557a89502e37db1bddd.title: Prohibition on performing a coordinating function
r-b557a89502e37db1bddd.requirement: Any person may not perform a coordinating function. The definition covers collecting competitively sensitive information from two or more owners for automated analysis used to set or recommend rental prices, material lease terms, or occupancy levels; setting those prices, terms, or levels through automated processing of another owner's competitively sensitive information; or setting or recommending those prices, terms, or levels for two or more owners through the same or substantially similar automated process that facilitates parallel pricing coordination. Processing includes using the information to train an algorithm.
r-b557a89502e37db1bddd.quoted_span: e.     any person to perform a coordinating function.

args.reason: The three alternative coordinating-function branches are not compiled. They require activity-specific facts about qualifying owners, competitively sensitive information, automated processing or training, set or recommended prices/terms/occupancy levels, and, for the third branch, parallel pricing coordination.

r-b557a89502e37db1bddd.exemptions: Excluded functions are providing, using, or collecting sensitive information solely for research, statistical analysis, or testing without using it to set or recommend current or future lease prices, terms, fees, or occupancy; developing a free publicly available rent estimate; using a qualifying equally available brokerage database that neither sets or recommends specified terms nor collects sensitive information to do so; and lawful government affordability-control activities. Specified institutional facilities are excluded from residential dwelling units.

Be It Enacted

e.     any person to perform a coordinating function.

“Coordinating function” means:
(1)   collecting the competitively sensitive
information of two or more rental property owners for the purpose of analyzing

providing, using, or collecting competitively sensitive

recommend rental prices, material lease terms, or occupancy rates or levels; or
(4)   a government entity setting or limiting rents or
sale prices of residential property through affordability controls in
accordance with the law.

“Competitively
sensitive information” means nonpublic information including, but not limited
to, prices, supply levels, security deposits, ideal occupancy levels, lease
contract termination, renewal dates of residential dwelling units, or any other
material lease terms.

“Nonpublic information” means information that is not
available to the public at no cost. In instances where the information is
combined with public information, all combined information shall be deemed
nonpublic information.

“Rental
property owner” means a person that owns, directly or indirectly, one or more
rental residential dwelling units.  Any person that holds a controlling
interest in an entity that owns a rental residential dwelling unit shall be
deemed to constitute a single rental property owner with that entity.

“Parallel pricing coordination” means a tacit or
express agreement between two or more rental property owners to raise, change,
maintain, or manipulate pricing for the leasing of reasonably interchangeable
residential dwelling units, unless required to do so in accordance with
affordability controls.  This includes agreements between a coordinator and
multiple property owners.

“Affordability controls” means a restriction on rent
price established pursuant to a government program, including but not limited

authorized pursuant to Subpart M of Part 982 of Title 24 of the Code of Federal

the “Fair Housing Act,” P.L.1985, c.222 (C.52:27D-301 et al.); any program

control or rent leveling ordinance; or other local, State, or federal
government housing program.

r-b9212520dd133bdf1584.title: Prohibition on obtaining coordinator services
r-b9212520dd133bdf1584.requirement: A rental property owner, or its agent, representative, or subcontractor, may not receive, subscribe to, contract for, or otherwise exchange consideration for the use of a coordinator's services.

args.reason: Statutory rental-property-owner status, the receipt or acquisition of services, and whether the service provider is a statutory coordinator are not fully compiled. Owner status includes direct or indirect ownership and the controlling-interest aggregation rule. Coordinator status requires operating the specified software or device and performing a coordinating function.

The algorithmic-device and coordinating-function exclusions have not been compiled for this services transaction. They include qualifying non-AI spreadsheets requiring human analysis, query-only databases, research/statistical analysis/testing without lease-setting use, free public rent estimates, qualifying brokerage databases, and lawful government affordability-control activities. These are definitional limitations, not blanket exemptions from other prohibited conduct.

r-b9212520dd133bdf1584.exemptions: Specified institutional facilities are excluded from residential dwelling units. Government entities acting through lawful affordability controls are excluded from coordinator status. Algorithmic-device and coordinating-function exclusions must be evaluated for the particular services.

Be It Enacted
by the Senate and General
Assembly of the State of New Jersey:

c.     two or more persons to engage in
1
or

1
parallel pricing coordination;

“Parallel pricing coordination” means a tacit or
express agreement between two or more rental property owners to raise, change,
maintain, or manipulate pricing for the leasing of reasonably interchangeable
residential dwelling units, unless required to do so in accordance with
affordability controls.  This includes agreements between a coordinator and
multiple property owners.

“Residential dwelling unit” means any house, apartment,
accessory unit, or other unit intended to be used as a primary residence in the
State. “Residential dwelling unit” shall not include inpatient medical care,
licensed long-term care, or detention or correctional facilities.

“Person” means, unless the context requires otherwise,
any natural person or persons, or any corporation, partnership, company, trust,
or association of persons.

“Tacit agreement” means mutual consent demonstrated
without verbal or written communication.  Mutual consent may, but need not, be
demonstrated by a pattern of conduct.

r-c243bf954944d60c4643.penalties: The conduct is a New Jersey Antitrust Act violation. Section 5 preserves application of C.56:9-6 through 9-17; specific penalties and remedies are not reproduced.
review_issues: All six categories were reviewed. The source supports algorithmic-rent-setting provisions but does not establish that New Jersey lacks rent-increase limits, just-cause eviction rules, security-deposit rules, application/screening-fee rules, or screening restrictions.
First-reprint markers and bracketed deleted language are preserved in exact quotations but are not treated as operative legal requirements.
No exclusive end date, later amendment, repeal, or superseding version is established by this source.
Section 5 preserves existing antitrust enforcement provisions, but their specific penalties and remedies are not reproduced.

Section 6(a) provides that the act does not authorize conduct already unlawful under the New Jersey Antitrust Act or any other law and is additional to that act. This savings provision does not establish a directional supersedes or conflicts_with interaction.
Section 8 authorizes discretionary Attorney General rulemaking; it does not require rulemaking or evidence an adopted implementing regulation.

Security deposits appear as competitively sensitive information, not as a separate deposit limit or handling requirement. References to government rent controls do not supply the substantive terms of those controls.
Several conduct-specific coverage conditions and definitional exclusions remain explicitly unsupported because they have not been compiled, rather than being assumed true or false.
Subsidized status alone does not establish that coordination is required by affordability controls.
The number of persons engaging in or facilitating the conduct is distinct from the ownership relationships in the underlying agreement.

The residential-unit definition turns on intended primary-residence use, not actual occupancy. Rental-property-owner status includes direct and indirect ownership and treats a controlling-interest holder and the owning entity as one owner.
